findings.title: A third catch-all-401 site was left open: resolveOwnerScope relabels any non-AuthError requireRole rejection as ScopeError('unauthorized', 401)
findings.arbiter_reasoning: Found by the Duty-4 sweep (rg 'instanceof AuthError' -A 6 over src/ and worker/, excluding __tests__). Structurally identical to the two sites fixed here. Every consumer maps ScopeError.statusCode straight onto the HTTP status: edit-reply-request.ts:79 and :186, import-offer/route.ts:132, past-replies/draft-status/route.ts:60-63, settings/postal-address/route.ts:91. A Postgres outage inside loadAppUser therefore still answers 401 {"error":"unauthorized"} on ~6 more owner routes and, being caught-and-returned rather than thrown, never reaches onRequestError, so Sentry stays silent. The intake's non_goals forbid touching other auth gates on this branch, so the proportionate outcome is a rejection-with-follow-up-issue or accepted-risk, not a scope widening; the arbiter decides.

findings.title: The change emits a new operator-actionable 5xx signal from 12 owner routes with no row in the alerting runbook
findings.arbiter_reasoning: The diff adds a terminal failure path: a DB/Redis fault behind requireRole now escapes 12 owner routes and is captured by onRequestError (src/instrumentation.ts:9). Duty 5 emits P1 when an emitted signal has no rule row. rg '1361|locations/add|owner-route|requireDashboardReviewOwner' over docs/runbooks/beta-launch-alerting.md returns nothing: no row, no filter, no triage entry, no grouping caveat. Rule 10 (beta-launch-alerting.md:472-495) is the exact precedent for this signal shape — an ADMIN_APP_URL request-fatal error captured through the same onRequestError — and it was discharged as a runbook REQUIREMENT with no Sentry rule installed. The proportionate remedy is the same: a Rule 12 requirement naming the emitted identity, the filter, the stack-grouping caveat and the operator's first move (Supabase/Upstash health).
